contradictions.what: Rep said they were asked for nothing they couldn't show ('Nothing, really. It was a clean one'), but later admitted dancing around PayPal and having no answer on Venmo.
'Clean one' conflicts with unfulfilled saved-card reference request and the engineer's 'we'll find out' at kickoff.
Rep says customer decided Venmo was a risk they'd take, yet no answer was ever given; customer's acceptance is the rep's assumption.
Daniel is named as decider who signed, but rep says their engineer sold the deal and Daniel's 'if' shifted after the engineer's prototype.
Rep says 'I know because the questions changed' about the Braintree call, then concedes not knowing what Braintree said; the call itself is inferred.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Answered 'Nothing, really. It was a clean one,' then admitted PayPal/Venmo evasion and an unfulfilled saved-card reference request when pressed.

dodges.question: What did we show them on PayPal/Venmo?
dodges.what: Hesitated ('...'), conceded 'We kind of danced around it' with no crisp Venmo answer.

outcome_signals.what: Daniel signed and finance signed what he brought: the deal closed as won.
Deal tipped from bake-off to committed after the weekend prototype.
PayPal/Venmo buttons were left unresolved and the customer accepted the risk; part of the business (Venmo/PayPal) may not have moved cleanly.
Saved-card migration at scale was not proven; deferred to implementation discovery.
